own_explanation.problem: Choose storage and architecture that fit a smaller computer while checking answer behavior separately. Packing fewer bits changes the saved numerical approximation; distillation changes a smaller student learning target and does not itself remove parameters.
own_explanation.branches_and_components: joint is the text/image/audio jointly trained source, and DPO is a preference comparison branch continued from it. PTQ of recommended joint is therefore distinct from distilling the chosen DPO teacher. A connector maps image/audio features into vectors the language core can receive; embedding maps input IDs to vectors; router selects experts. The current model uses RMSNorm for feature magnitude adjustment. PTQ packs non-router Linear weights, while embedding, normalization, bias and router stay FP32; each output-weight row has one saved quantization scale.
own_explanation.new_rmsnorm_background: In the newly read 14.2, one row is one token position and its columns are features. For d features x_i, the illustrated RMS scale is sqrt((sum_i x_i^2)/d + eps), where eps=1e-5 avoids division by zero; each original x_i is divided by this scale. Mean subtraction is absent. [2,2,2] has mean square 4 and RMS about 2, so it becomes about [1,1,1]. [1,2,3] has mean square 14/3, RMS about 2.1602, and scaled values about [0.4629,0.9258,1.3887]. LayerNorm instead subtracts mean 2, giving all zeros for the first row and about [-1.2247,0,1.2247] for the second after its standard-deviation scaling. gamma is a learned feature multiplier and beta a learned offset; the example fixes gamma=1 and LayerNorm beta=0. The code mean(-1,keepdim=True) selects each row feature axis and preserves a one-column denominator. This scale acts on features, whereas quantization scales map integer weight codes back toward their floating weights. I did not run the normalization code or its experiment links.
own_explanation.code_input_and_output: The assigned code seeds one Linear(8,4) layer, quantizes those weights at four bits, and feeds one all-ones row. Both results have shape (1,4). The max absolute difference only concerns that input. Original bytes are (32+4)*4=144. Quantized payload is 32*4/8=16 for weights plus 4*4=16 scales and 4*4=16 biases, total 48. The preserved first CPU run gave maximum difference 0.046346306800842285. At eight bits weight storage is 32 bytes and total payload is 64; the preserved exercise result was 0.0037038326263427734. I compared current script bytes to those actual executions, rather than running again.
own_explanation.formula: KD uses 0.5 CE + 0.5 T^2 KL(p_T||q_T), T=2. CE uses the true-answer target. Teacher p_T and student q_T come from their corresponding candidate scores divided by the same T and then softmax. KL is sum_i p_i(log p_i-log q_i), so teacher probabilities provide the weighting and candidate columns must correspond. The helper already multiplies by T^2=4; the caller only uses the 0.5 mixture weight and must not add a second factor of four. Only the student is updated. This loss scale is distinct from a whole-question correctness rate.
own_explanation.relevant_numbers: The prose cites joint FP32/4-bit/8-bit files of 1,345,023/275,381/429,365 bytes and tensor payloads of 1,312,512/248,864/402,720, all at 78/90 whole-question correctness. One four-bit generated ID sequence changes even at the same score; eight-bit has no observed change on these questions. The DPO four-bit comparison changes two sequences at the same score. The width-48 two-layer Dense student has 79,920 parameters and 319,680 FP32 tensor bytes. CE and KD share an initial student, seed/batch rules, 350 updates and 145,163 effective answer positions. Both validation counts are 59/84, but final CE/KD counts are 62/90 and 61/90. KD four-bit storage is 91,680 tensor bytes, with cited file 106,229, and remains at 61/90 despite six changed outputs/actions on already wrong questions. I did not recreate these full-model experiments.
own_explanation.how_to_interpret_task_counts: The paired fractions list CE before KD. Full loops require correct model request, actual calculator execution and correct final model answer: 1/12 versus 0/12. Independent refill supplies question and tool result without the first request, scoring 1/6 for each. Copying requires exact specified digits (0/3 each); shape identifies square versus circle from the image (0/9 each). All are subsets of the same 90-question examination, not extra questions. The CE/KD 1+8 example shows wrong request parameters and wrong reading of the true result as separate failures.
own_explanation.how_to_check: For the assigned exercise, keep the same seed/layer/input and change only bits=8; count packed weights separately from scale/bias overhead and compare the print lines. For background RMSNorm understanding, hand-calculate squared-feature mean and square root, then compare the no-centering result with LayerNorm; adding a shared offset need not be removed by RMSNorm. For full saved deployments, storage, final answers, runtime memory and speed require distinct evidence, so small-file observations alone do not settle the others.
